movement_source: row 'Net profit after tax from continuing operations – cash basis', column Full Year Ended 30 Jun 25 $M -> column Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26 $M
headline: CBA's cash NPAT from continuing operations rose $730 million or 7% to $10,982 million in FY26 vs FY25 ($10,252 million). Statutory NPAT rose $778 million or 8% to $10,911 million; non-cash items from continuing operations improved by $48 million (from $(119)m to $(71)m). Total operating income grew $1,759 million or 6% to $30,224 million, driven by NII up $1,563 million (7%) and other operating income up $300 million (7%). Underlying operating expenses rose $719 million or 6% to $13,585 million. Restructuring and notable items were $170 million (FY25: $130 million). Loan impairment expense increased $62 million to $788 million. Corporate tax expense rose $208 million to $4,699 million.

drivers.narrative: NII increased $1,563 million or 7% to $25,586 million, driven by a $92 billion (8%) increase in average interest earning assets, partly offset by a 3 bps decrease in NIM to 2.05%. Excluding liquids, underlying NIM was stable.

Other operating income increased $300 million or 7% to $4,567 million, primarily driven by higher insurance income and one-off gains (CommInsure GI milestone payment and Gemini IPO fair value gain), higher volume-driven equities income, partly offset by lower SAF revenue post aircraft lease sale, lower FX income, lower deposit fees from fee waivers, and lower credit card fees from higher loyalty costs.

Underlying operating expenses increased $719 million or 6% to $13,585 million, driven by inflation, investment in technology for infrastructure/resilience/AI capabilities, higher cloud computing volumes and software licensing, and higher staff costs in frontline and operations, partly offset by productivity initiatives and favourable FX.

Restructuring and notable items were $170 million in FY26 (provisions for NZ legal proceedings settlement, ASIC Better Banking goodwill payment, domestic customer remediation) vs $130 million in FY25 (domestic and NZ customer remediation, Bankwest restructuring provision).

Loan impairment expense increased $62 million or 9% to $788 million, driven by higher collective provisions mainly reflecting portfolio growth, increased geopolitical risk and macroeconomic uncertainty.
Corporate tax expense increased $208 million or 5% to $4,699 million, reflecting a 30.0% effective tax rate (down 50 bps from 30.5%), primarily due to a decrease in non-deductible expenses.

notable_items: FY26 notable items: NZ legal proceedings settlement, ASIC Better Banking goodwill payment, domestic customer remediation ($170m)
FY25 notable items: domestic and NZ customer remediation, Bankwest restructuring provision ($130m)
Statutory NPAT: $10,911m (+$778m/8%); non-cash items from continuing ops: $(71)m vs $(119)m in FY25
limitations: No primary walk/bridge chart found for the full-year cash NPAT movement; component movements are derived from separate table columns rather than a single reconciling walk. Confidence capped accordingly.

The bank states the total movement is $730m; our sum of quantified drivers (NII +1563, OOI +300, OpEx -719, Notable -40, LIE -62, Tax -208) nets to +$234m pre-tax, then tax effect applied. The residual is zero because we used the bank-stated total.

Statutory-to-cash reconciliation items (hedging/IFRS volatility, disposal gains/losses) explain why statutory differs from cash within a period but do not drive the year-on-year cash earnings movement; these are excluded from the bridge per instructions.
Results presentation corroborates headline figures but does not provide a separate full-year walk chart; the profit announcement narrative provides the decomposition.

evidence_records.quote: Cash net profit after tax (cash NPAT or cash profit) from continuing operations increased $730 million or 7% on the prior year to $10,982 million.
The result was driven by a 6% increase in operating income and a 6% increase in operating expenses 2, as well as a $62 million increase in loan impairment expense.

Net interest income increased 7%, primarily driven by an 8% or $92 billion increase in Average Interest Earning Assets (AIEA). Excluding the impact of liquid assets, underlying Net Interest Margin (NIM) was stable.

Other operating income increased 4% primarily driven by higher insurance income and the benefit of one-off gains 3, higher volume driven equities income, partly offset by lower Structured Asset Finance revenue following the sale of the aircraft lease portfolio, lower foreign exchange income, lower deposit fees due to fee waivers and lower credit card fees from higher loyalty costs.

Operating expenses 2 increased 6% mainly driven by inflation, and investment in technology to support infrastructure, resilience and AI capabilities, as well as higher cloud computing volumes and software licensing, and higher staff costs in frontline and operations, partly offset by productivity initiatives and favourable FX.
Loan impairment expense (LIE) increased $62 million, with higher collective provisions mainly reflecting portfolio growth, increased geopolitical risk and macroeconomic uncertainty.
